data.long_meaning: Derived from Old Norse, Sigrid means 'victory-rule'. This name was popular among the Vikings, symbolizing strength and victory. The name Sigrid carries the meaning “Victory-rule” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Sigrid usually hope their child will grow to embody victory-rule and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sigrid total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sigrid holds a significant cultural impact, particularly in Scandinavian history and folklore. Sigrid is a name with Norse roots and was popular among the Vikings. It symbolizes strength, victory, and the power of the feminine spirit, reflecting the warrior culture of the ancient Scandinavians.
data.spiritual_significance: Sigrid's name carries a deeper spiritual significance, representing triumph over challenges and adversity. It is a reminder of the power of the divine within us, and the ability to overcome obstacles through courage, resilience, and determination. In a spiritual context, Sigrid embodies the goddess Freyja, who is associated with victory, beauty, and fertility. Carrying this name can serve as a source of inspiration, reminding us of our inner strength and the power to triumph over challenges in our lives.
